storyboard.claim: The laurel's rewards are real food and blankets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gift icon: the prize as something handed out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the laurel segment on the rewards themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the actual goods, not just a prize.
storyboard.staging: Host talking beside the gift icon: the reward is physical food, not a title.

storyboard.claim: The rewards decide between misery and a little comfort.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow slumped in the dust of the mines, worn out by the cold and hunger the rewards would ease.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the food to the people who go without it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the misery the narrator describes as a body, not a list.
storyboard.staging: Darrow slumps in the mine, worried: he lives in the misery the reward could ease.

storyboard.claim: The magistrate hands out a cheap, fake gold laurel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon: the laurel as the prize everyone fights over.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rewards to the object that decides who gets them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The laurel is a prize, and the callout says it is cheap and fake.
storyboard.staging: Host holds up the trophy: the laurel is a cheap prize, not a real reward.

storyboard.claim: Darrow's raw count beat every other clan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow celebrating his record haul in the mine.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the prize to the man who earned it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the record a face: he deserved the laurel.
storyboard.staging: Darrow celebrates: his output was the best, so the win is genuine warmth.

storyboard.claim: The laurel goes to Gamma despite Lambda producing the most fuel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan, the Gold guard, holds the trophy as the arbitrary choice is made.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Darrow's record to the arbitrary award.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the Gold enforcer behind the decision.
storyboard.staging: Gold guard with a sneer: the award is a rigged choice made by the Golds.

storyboard.claim: Gamma eats while Lambda starves, again and again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow slumped in the mine while the reward is handed to others.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the award to the cost it imposes on Lambda.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the repeated starving a body the viewer can read.
storyboard.staging: Darrow sad and slumped: Lambda starves while Gamma eats.

storyboard.claim: The Golds run a rigged system and the cruelty is the purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan, the Gold guard, smirking with cold control.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the single award to the system behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the cruelty on a face: the sinister charm of the Gold guard.
storyboard.staging: Gold guard smirks: the cruelty is deliberate, not an accident.

storyboard.claim: Shifting goalposts mean hard work cannot win.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow thinking hard, worried, about a game he cannot win.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the cruelty to what the system does to effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: The worried thinker shows effort with no reward.
storyboard.staging: Darrow worried and thinking: working hard does not win in this system.

storyboard.claim: The system is like a toxic gig economy at life-or-death stakes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the comparison is the point, no icon needed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the award to the modern comparison the hosts draw.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the comparison in the narrator's words.
storyboard.staging: Host talks directly: he is drawing the modern parallel.

storyboard.claim: Delivery apps reward punishing hours with status that can change at any time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the 14-hour figure is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the comparison to its concrete example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact number of hours the example uses.
storyboard.staging: Host speaking; the callout carries the 14-hour detail.

callout.text: KEEP YOU RUNNING ON THE TREADMILL

storyboard.claim: The algorithm keeps workers running on a treadmill.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow walking the mine treadmill, worried.
storyboard.onScreenText: KEEP YOU RUNNING ON THE TREADMILL
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the example to the mechanism that drives it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the treadmill a body in motion that never gets anywhere.
storyboard.staging: Darrow walks worried: he is kept running in place.

storyboard.claim: The system keeps the Reds fighting each other instead of their bosses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow fights the rebel leader, the Reds turned against each other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the treadmill to the tribal hatred it breeds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two Reds in a real fight, not a single angry man.
storyboard.staging: Darrow punches toward a Red who fights back: the neighbors are fighting each other.

storyboard.claim: The laurel breeds deep hatred between the clans.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the hatred is in the callout's words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the fight to its root in the laurel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the hatred as the intended output of the game.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks: the laurel is designed to make clans hate each other.

storyboard.claim: Lambda hates Gamma, not the Golds who hoard the wealth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow pointing angrily at the rival clan.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the breeding of hatred to who the hatred is aimed at.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point shows Lambda's target is the rival clan.
storyboard.staging: Darrow points angrily at Gamma: the anger is aimed at the wrong people.

storyboard.claim: Lambda hates the Gamma miners for one extra ration of sugar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the sugar detail is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the target of the hatred to the small thing that fuels it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tiny reward makes the hatred look absurd.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks about the sugar; the text carries the detail.

storyboard.claim: A young Gamma boy's toes slip from the grav lift railing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the scene is carried by its callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the sugar to the scene in the grav lift.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact detail of the accident.
storyboard.staging: Host talks; the callout names the toes and the railing.

storyboard.claim: The boy is left floating, helpless and terrified, in zero gravity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A figure tipped and floating in the shaft, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the toes to the boy losing his footing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face and the airborne body make the terror readable.
storyboard.staging: A figure floats, afraid: the anti-gravity has left him helpless.

storyboard.claim: The older Lambda miners do not help and mock the boy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rebel leader points and smirks at the falling child.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the boy's fear to the adults who laugh at it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk gives the mockery its cruel edge.
storyboard.staging: The Red leader points and smirks: the adults mock the child.

storyboard.claim: The Reds mock each other and police each other for the Golds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rebel leader points angrily at a fellow Red.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the mockery to what it accomplishes for the Golds.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry point shows the Reds enforcing the system on each other.
storyboard.staging: The Red leader points in anger: the Reds police each other.

storyboard.claim: The hosts test the logic from the Gold side.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking through the economics.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the mockery to a question about the economics.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next question as a logic test.
storyboard.staging: Host thinks: he is working through the economics.

storyboard.claim: A mining operation would normally reward its highest producer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking through the capitalist logic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the hosts' question to the logic they are testing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the expected logic of a mine operator.
storyboard.staging: Host poses the expected economics: pay the top producer.

storyboard.claim: Darrow pulled a record 9,000 kilos of helium 3.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow celebrating his record haul.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the logic to the record that should be rewarded.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact record number.
storyboard.staging: Darrow celebrates: the record is genuine, so the warmth is earned.

callout.text: WHY NOT GIVE LAMBDA THE LAUREL?

storyboard.claim: Why would the Golds not reward Lambda to push output?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host asking the question.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHY NOT GIVE LAMBDA THE LAUREL?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the record to the question it raises.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the question in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Host asks the question directly.

storyboard.claim: The Golds are not capitalists, so the capitalist logic fails.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host speaking; the struck phrase carries the rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the question to the answer that rejects the logic.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the capitalist label.
storyboard.staging: Host rejects the label: the strike carries it, no icon.

storyboard.claim: The Golds are feudal lords with more wealth than they can spend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, the Gold student, smirks in a Gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rejected label to the correct one.
storyboard.addedInformation: A Gold face with an edge shows the lordly self-regard.
storyboard.staging: Titus smirks: the feudal lord's charm with an edge.

storyboard.claim: Maintaining absolute, unquestioned dominance is the Golds' real aim.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one person controlling many.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the feudal lords to the control they keep.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer shows control over others, not just wealth.
storyboard.staging: Titus smirks beside the puppeteer: the Golds control the Reds.

storyboard.claim: Rewarding merit would be a social contract the Golds refuse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking about the contract.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dominance to the contract it would imply.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the contract the Golds will not sign.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks about the contract.

storyboard.claim: Paying for merit would give the Reds leverage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking about leverage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the contract to the leverage it creates.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the Reds would gain power from a fair deal.
storyboard.staging: Host explains the leverage.

storyboard.claim: If Reds realize their labor commands a price, the system breaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow surprised, realising his labor has value.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the leverage to the realisation it would bring.
storyboard.addedInformation: The surprised face shows the spark of the realisation.
storyboard.staging: Darrow is surprised: the Reds would see their own value.

storyboard.claim: The Golds rig the math to show godlike power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking about the rigged math.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the realisation to the Golds' answer to it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the rigging as the demonstration of power.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks about rigging.

storyboard.claim: The Golds assert that merit means nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan, the Gold guard, points down at the Reds with a sneer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rigging to the message it sends.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point shows the Gold guard deciding who eats.
storyboard.staging: Gold guard points with a sneer: the Gold decides who eats.

storyboard.claim: Deciding who eats on a whim reinforces the caste hierarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains beside Darrow slumped in the mine.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the Gold guard's message to the caste it holds in place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains show the hierarchy as a bond on the Reds.
storyboard.staging: Darrow slumps under the chains: the hierarchy binds him.

storyboard.claim: The laurel is a psychological weapon, not a performance incentive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking: the weapon is named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the hierarchy to the tool that keeps it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Calls the laurel a weapon rather than an incentive.
storyboard.staging: Host names the weapon; the callout carries it.

storyboard.claim: The laurel reminds the Reds they are powerless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow slumped, sad, in the mine.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the weapon to the feeling it leaves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump makes the powerlessness a body.
storyboard.staging: Darrow slumps sad: he feels utterly powerless.

storyboard.claim: The story of the game is the real cage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains: the cage made literal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the powerlessness to the story that holds it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the cage is the story, not the game.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks; the chains show the cage.

storyboard.claim: Exhaustion leaves no mental room to ask why they are trapped.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow worried, thinking hard about the next race.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the cage to the exhaustion that keeps people in it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The thinking worry shows the mind occupied.
storyboard.staging: Darrow thinks worried: he has no room to question the system.

storyboard.claim: Gamification alone is not enough, exhaustion must be given a sacred purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking about the purpose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the exhaustion to the purpose laid over it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the purpose the system gives its people.
storyboard.staging: Host explains the purpose.

storyboard.claim: Life expectancy is about 25 years if lucky.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass: short time running out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the purpose to the short lives it must justify.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass shows the short life as time running out.
storyboard.staging: Host with an hourglass: life is short for the Reds.

storyboard.claim: Friends are crushed or killed, and their suffering is scripted as a religious duty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon beside a sad Darrow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the short life to the deaths it hides.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave makes the death of friends concrete.
storyboard.staging: Darrow sad beside the grave: the dead are given a religious meaning.

storyboard.claim: Pierce Brown illustrates the indoctrination, so the township must be visualised.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, introducing the township scenes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the grave to the township scenes that follow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the indoctrination as the subject of the next scene.
storyboard.staging: Host introduces the township.
